citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (2020). EPANET 2.2 User Manual. Office of Research and Development, Cincinnati, OH. https://usepa.github.io/EPANET2.2/
description: EPANET performs extended-period simulation of the hydraulic and water quality behaviour of pressurised drinking water distribution networks made of pipes, junctions, pumps, valves, storage tanks and reservoirs. It tracks the flow in each pipe, the pressure at each node, the water level in each tank, a chemical concentration, water age and source tracing over a simulation period, with pressure-dependent demands, rule-based controls, several head-loss formulas and no limit on network size. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency developed it to understand the movement and fate of drinking water constituents; engineers use it to design and size infrastructure, retrofit ageing systems, optimise tanks and pumps, reduce energy use, investigate water quality, prepare for emergencies, and model contamination threats and resilience to security threats or natural disasters. It is generic and runs any network described in an INP input file. EPA's official release is version 2.2 (July 2020): a Windows program with a visual network editor, a Windows toolkit library, source code and a user manual in English and Spanish. The solver engine and its C toolkit are developed further as OWA-EPANET by the Open Water Analytics community, whose release 2.3.5 (February 2026) builds on Linux, macOS and Windows but has no graphical interface. Licence: EPA's EPANET page calls EPANET public domain software; EPA's release repository and OWA-EPANET state the MIT licence; either way it is free and unrestricted. Caveats: EPA's official release and the community engine differ in version and features. Simulation uses are network flow, capacity planning, emergency response and resilience of water supply. Related tools not yet catalogued: EPANET-MSX (multi-species reactions) and EPANET-RTX (real-time models) from EPA, and WNTR, which wraps EPANET for resilience analysis.
